newsitem.title: USA: Tribune posts 18 percent gain in net income.
newsitem.headline: Tribune posts 18 percent gain in net income.

text.p: Tribune Co. said Friday it earned $66 million in the third quarter, a gain of 18 percent from a year earlier, on a 12 percent increase in revenue.

Tribune, which owns the Chicago Tribune, television and radio outlets and the Chicago Cubs baseball team, said the earnings amounted to $1 a share, up from $56 million, or 79 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Sales grew to $618 million from $552 million.

Broadcasting and entertainment operating profit rose 18 percent, due mainly to improvements at the Cubs and in the radio group, the company said. Tribune agreed in July to acquire Renaissance Communications Corp., which owns six television stations.
Tribune said operating profit in its publishing jumped 17 percent, due to gains from all newspapers.
Tribune's education group reported operating profit of $22 million compared with $3 million in 1995, due to contributions from recent acquisitions.

"These results reflect a different Tribune," Chairman John Madigan said. "We've changed dramatically in recent years. We're making a major move in broadcasting with the pending acquisition of Renaissance, and we're developing a very exciting education business that is not dependent on advertising."
Advertising revenues increased 6 percent, while newsprint and ink expense fell 14 percent, as average newsprint prices fell 10 percent.

Tribune owns and operates 10 television and five radio stations, publishes four daily newspapers, produces and syndicates programming and information, and provides educational products and services for schools and consumers.

For the first nine months, Tribune earned $290 million, or $4.50 a share, on sales of $1.80 billion, compared with $206 million, or $2.94 a share, on sales of $1.65 billion in the comparable 1995 period.
